issues.legal_issue: A person claiming an interest in compensation may be joined in a land acquisition reference when the objection before the court is likely to affect that interest.
material_facts: The acquired land was leased, and the compensation was apportioned between the landowner and the lessee.
The landowner and lessee each sought a reference challenging compensation and its apportionment.
A decree-holder had attached the lessee’s share of the compensation and claimed an interest in it.
The decree-holder’s claim could be affected by the resolution of the objections in the references.
issues.conclusion: The decree-holder was a person interested in the compensation and in the objections, and was entitled to be made a party to the references.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3(b), 20 and 21 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the inclusive definition of “person interested” covers a person claiming an interest in compensation, even without an interest in the acquired land. Such a person is interested in an objection concerning the amount or apportionment of compensation if the decision is likely to affect the person’s claim. Section 21 excludes consideration of interests not affected by the objection, but does not restrict the grounds an affected person may raise to protect those interests. The Court followed Grant v. State of Bihar and relied on Golap Khan v. Bholanath Marick and Siva Pratapa Bhattadu v. A.E.L. Mission; it distinguished Manjoor Ahmed v. Rajlaxmi Dasi, Abu Bakar v. Peary Mohan Mukherjee, Gobinda Kumar Roy v. Debendra Kumar Roy Chowdhury, Mahammad Safi v. Haran Chandra and Karuna Sindhu Dhar v. Panna Lal Paramanik.

rule.if: land_acquisition_reference and claims_interest_in_compensation and (objection_concerns_amount_or_apportionment) and claim_likely_affected

predicates.land_acquisition_reference: A court is determining objections in a reference concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.claims_interest_in_compensation: A person claims an interest in the compensation to be awarded or apportioned.
predicates.objection_concerns_amount_or_apportionme: An objection before the court concerns the amount or apportionment of compensation.
predicates.claim_likely_affected: The decision on the objection is likely to affect the person’s claimed interest in compensation.
predicates.may_be_joined_as_party: The person may be joined as a party to the reference.

issues.definition: When a person claims an interest in compensation and an objection in a land acquisition reference is likely to affect that interest, the person may be joined as a party.

issues.legal_issue: A person whose interest is affected by objections in a land acquisition reference may raise points that protect that interest, including a challenge to a compromise, unless the points are expressly barred.
material_facts: A decree-holder had attached the lessee’s share of the compensation in execution of a decree and later withdrew the amount subject to an undertaking to hold it as directed by the court.
The landowner and lessee filed a compromise in the pending references, and the decree-holder alleged that the compromise would defeat the attachment and execution of the decree.
The objections in the references concerned compensation and its apportionment, and their resolution could affect the decree-holder’s interest.
issues.conclusion: The decree-holder could raise all points protecting interests affected by the objections, and could not be barred from challenging the compromise on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 20 and 21 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the court considers the interests of persons affected by the objections; section 21 does not restrict the grounds such persons may raise to protect those interests. The Court applied its interpretation of these provisions and, consistently with the approach in Grant v. State of Bihar, favoured resolving related points in the same proceeding where they are not expressly barred.

rule.if: land_acquisition_reference and person_interest_affected_by_objections and proposed_point_protects_that_interest and point_not_expressly_barred

predicates.land_acquisition_reference: A court is determining objections in a reference concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.person_interest_affected_by_objections: A person’s claimed interest is affected by the objections being determined.
predicates.proposed_point_protects_that_interest: The person seeks to raise a point to protect that affected interest.
predicates.point_not_expressly_barred: No applicable restriction expressly bars the person from raising the point.

issues.definition: A person affected by objections in a land acquisition reference may raise a point to protect that interest if the point is not expressly barred.

issues.legal_issue: A revision is competent against an order in a land acquisition reference that is not an award when no appeal lies and the lower court has refused to exercise jurisdiction or acted with material irregularity.
material_facts: The Civil Judge rejected applications to add the decree-holder as a party while the references were still pending.
The orders did not determine the references or constitute awards.
No appeal lay against the orders, and the Civil Judge had refused to exercise jurisdiction over the applications.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could entertain the revisions because the orders were not awards, no appeal lay, and the Civil Judge had refused to exercise jurisdiction vested in that court.
issues.legal_principle: Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, provides for appeals from awards; the orders refusing joinder were not awards. Where no appeal lies, section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, permits revision when the lower court has refused to exercise jurisdiction vested in it or acted with material irregularity in exercising jurisdiction. Section 53 of the Land Acquisition Act makes the Code applicable to proceedings before the court, as relevant here.

rule.if: revision_from_land_acquisition_reference_order and order_not_an_award and no_appeal_lies and (lower_court_refused_jurisdiction or lower_court_committed_material_irregularity)

predicates.revision_from_land_acquisition_reference: A revision challenges an order made by a court in a land acquisition reference.
predicates.order_not_an_award: The challenged order does not constitute an award determining the reference.
predicates.no_appeal_lies: No appeal is available against the challenged order.
predicates.lower_court_refused_jurisdiction: The lower court refused to exercise jurisdiction vested in it.
predicates.lower_court_committed_material_irregular: The lower court acted with material irregularity in exercising its jurisdiction.
predicates.high_court_revision_is_competent: The High Court may entertain the revision.

issues.definition: A revision from an order in a land acquisition reference is competent when the order is not an award, no appeal lies, and the lower court refused jurisdiction or committed material irregularity.
